Introduction

Minnesota’s Home Care Provider — Basic License allows you to provide non-medical home care services. The MN Department of Health (MDH) oversees licensing under the Home Care Bill of Rights.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Minnesota’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Minnesota’s Regulations

MDH issues Basic and Comprehensive home care licenses. The Basic License covers non-medical services. Requirements include state licensing, background studies, training standards, and quality monitoring.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Basic License services include homemaker, companion, personal care, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the MN Secretary of State, apply for Basic License through MDH, complete background study requirements, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Minnesota benchmarks: Private pay rates $24-$34/hour, PCA program rates $18-$24/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling software, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

Minnesota requires background studies through NETStudy 2.0 and training per MDH standards.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting MDH requirements including the Home Care Bill of Rights.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build referral networks in the Twin Cities metro and greater Minnesota communities.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing, training records, and compliance with the Home Care Bill of Rights.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between Basic and Comprehensive licenses? Basic covers non-medical services; Comprehensive includes nursing and therapy services.
